text: A farmer carries 12 eggs and drops 3, which smash. How many are still whole?
Three hens and one dog are in a yard. How many legs between them?
why: Three hens have 6 legs and the dog has 4.

text: Halve 40, then halve it again. What's left?
Your bus sets off at 10:45 and the ride lasts 50 minutes. When do you get off?
why: 10:45 plus 15 minutes is 11:00, plus 35 more is 11:35.

text: Which is bigger: three quarters, or two thirds?
why: Three quarters is 9/12; two thirds is only 8/12.

text: Six hours is a quarter of a day. How many minutes is that?
why: A quarter of a day is 6 hours, and 6 × 60 = 360.

text: Unscramble LIPNCE to find something you write with.
Pick any starting figure. Double it, add 6, halve the result, then subtract your starting figure. What remains, whatever you picked?
why: Doubling then halving cancels out, leaving just half of the 6.

text: Spot the one that is not prime: 2, 3, 5, 9, 11, 13.
why: All the others are prime numbers; 9 is 3 × 3.

text: You drive 60 miles at 30 mph, then 60 miles back at 60 mph. What's your average speed for the whole trip, in mph?
why: 120 miles in 3 hours (2 there, 1 back) is 40 mph, not 45.

text: At a party, everyone shakes hands with everyone else once, and there are 28 handshakes. How many people are there?
15 people get off a bus and 10 get on, leaving 25 aboard. How many were on to start with?
A £20 shirt is cut by 10%, then cut by 10% again. What does it cost now?
why: £20 → £18 → £16.20; the second cut is 10% of £18, not of £20.
